clinicalPearls: A very common, benign, self-limiting eruption of the term newborn, typically appearing in the first few days of life and rarely present at birth.
Lesions are blotchy erythematous macules with central urticarial papules, vesicles or pustules, giving the classic flea-bitten appearance.
The palms and soles are characteristically spared, reflecting the eruption's association with hair follicles which are absent at those sites.
The eruption waxes and wanes and migrates over different body regions over hours to days, then resolves without sequelae.
Wright or Giemsa stain of a pustule shows abundant eosinophils, and a peripheral blood eosinophilia may accompany florid cases.
It is more frequent in term and post-term, larger infants and is uncommon in the preterm, which helps in bedside reasoning.
Diagnosis is clinical; the well appearance of the infant and characteristic morphology distinguish it from serious infective causes of neonatal pustules.
No treatment is required and parents should be reassured, but atypical, persistent or pustular eruptions in an unwell neonate warrant a septic and viral screen.
reference.pathophysiology: Erythema toxicum neonatorum is a benign inflammatory dermatosis of the newborn whose precise trigger is unknown. Histology shows an eosinophil-rich infiltrate centred on the pilosebaceous unit, with eosinophils and some neutrophils accumulating in the upper follicle and adjacent dermis, and pustules forming in a subcorneal or intrafollicular location. The follicular localisation explains sparing of the palms and soles. Current thinking favours an innate immune or transient inflammatory response, possibly reflecting activation of the neonatal immune system on early microbial colonisation of the skin and hair follicles after birth, rather than any toxic, infective or allergic process. The condition is entirely reactive and leaves no residual pigmentary or scarring change.
additionalInvestigations: Wright or Giemsa stain of pustule contents showing predominant eosinophils
Gram stain and bacterial culture to exclude staphylococcal infection when unwell
viral swabs and PCR for herpes simplex if vesicular and clinical suspicion exists
potassium hydroxide preparation to exclude candidal pustulosis
full blood count where peripheral eosinophilia is being assessed
septic screen including blood culture if the neonate is systemically unwell
skin biopsy only in atypical or diagnostically uncertain presentations
redFlags: an unwell, febrile or poorly feeding neonate, which is inconsistent with benign erythema toxicum
grouped vesicles, especially on the scalp or presenting part, raising concern for neonatal herpes simplex
pustules with a positive Gram stain or culture indicating bacterial infection
lesions present at birth or persisting beyond the expected transient course
involvement of palms and soles, which is atypical and should prompt reconsideration
reference.prognosis: The prognosis is excellent; the eruption is entirely benign and resolves spontaneously within days to a couple of weeks, leaving no scarring or pigmentary change, and recurrence is unusual.
pitfalls: mistaking the benign eruption for neonatal sepsis or, conversely, dismissing true infection as erythema toxicum in an unwell baby
failing to consider neonatal herpes simplex when vesicles are present
over-investigating a well term infant with classic morphology
confusing it with transient neonatal pustular melanosis, which is present at birth and leaves pigmented macules
not recognising that palm and sole involvement argues against the diagnosis
management: No specific treatment required, as the eruption is entirely benign and self-limiting; parental reassurance is the mainstay
Avoidance of unnecessary investigation or antibiotics once the clinical diagnosis is secure
Bedside confirmation with a Wright or Giemsa stain of pustule contents showing predominant eosinophils where the diagnosis is uncertain
Exclusion of infective mimics such as staphylococcal pustulosis, herpes simplex and candidal infection if the neonate is systemically unwell
Routine gentle skin care with observation for spontaneous resolution over days to a couple of weeks
